statement: A rule that withholds by falling back to an older, more generous reading hands out credit, so a withhold needs evidence as strong as a claim, and must be said. A prospective rubric's test-count rules were made to withhold wherever their condition might not hold: on any mention of a tool setting in any configuration file or CI workflow (comments, echo strings and default values included), and on almost any use of a cleared list. Each withhold restored the calibrated rubric's full credit with nothing in the note, and an adversarial review found the commonest deselect-everything hook scored verified again. Rule: withhold only on evidence the condition is really in force (an active key in a section the tool reads, a flag on a command line that runs it, a statement that demonstrably restores what was removed), treat a value that leaves the default reading as the default, and say every withhold in the output in one bounded clause naming the rule and the reason.

When a run's branch was pre-pushed at main and the push hook accepts only a fast-forward of it, a card's instruction to put the branch on an older PR's head cannot be followed as written; with merge, cherry-pick and am behind approval, the only faithful route left is to lay the old PR's content over main by hand and prove the port mechanically: the old PR's diff against its base and the port's diff against main must match file for file in numstat, and main's own changes must reappear against the old head on every file both sides touched. Rule: when history operations are unavailable, port by content, verify both directions by numstat before committing, and name the original commits and the reason in the port's commit message and the hand-back.
